I'll solve this problem directly. Let me work through it carefully.

## Setup

Place the frustum's axis along the $z$-axis: lower base is the disk $x^2+y^2\le 16$ at $z=0$ (radius 4), upper base is $x^2+y^2\le 1$ at $z=5$ (radius 1). The radius at height $z$ is $R(z)=4-\tfrac{3}{5}z$.

## Finding the cutting plane

By rotational symmetry, the plane (tangent to both base-disks and cutting all generators) can be taken parallel to the $y$-axis: $x=\alpha z+\beta$.

**Tangency to lower base** ($z=0$): the line $x=\beta$ must be tangent to the disk $x^2+y^2\le 16$, so $\beta=\pm 4$. Take $\beta=4$ (tangent point $(4,0,0)$).

**Tangency to upper base** ($z=5$): $x=5\alpha+4$ tangent to $x^2+y^2\le 1$, so $(5\alpha+4)^2=1$, giving $\alpha=-\tfrac35$ or $\alpha=-1$.

A generator at angle $\theta$ runs from $(4\cos\theta,4\sin\theta,0)$ to $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta,5)$, with $x(z)=\cos\theta\,(4-\tfrac35 z)$. The plane intersects it where
$$\cos\theta\,(4-\tfrac35 z)=\alpha z+4.$$

- **$\alpha=-\tfrac35$**: gives $(\cos\theta-1)(4-\tfrac35 z)=0$, so for $\theta\ne 0$ the only solution is $z=\tfrac{20}{3}\notin[0,5]$ — the plane is parallel to all generators, not cutting them. **Rejected.**
- **$\alpha=-1$**: gives $z=\dfrac{20(1-\cos\theta)}{5-3\cos\theta}\in[0,5]$ for all $\theta$ (equals $0$ at $\theta=0$, equals $5$ at $\theta=\pi$). **Cuts all elements.** ✓

So the plane is $\boxed{x+z=4}$.

## Computing the volumes

At height $z$, the cross-section is a disk of radius $R=4-\tfrac35 z$; the plane gives the line $x=4-z$. Set $c=4-z$. The **upper part** ($x+z\ge 4$, i.e. $x\ge c$) has circular-segment area
$$A_{\text{up}}(z)=R^2\arccos\!\tfrac{c}{R}-c\sqrt{R^2-c^2}.$$

Check regimes: $c-R=-\tfrac25 z<0$ for $z>0$ (always a right segment), $c+R=8(1-\tfrac z5)>0$ for $z<5$ (never the full disk). Good — segment regime throughout $(0,5)$.

Substitute $t=z/5\in[0,1]$: $R=4-3t$, $c=4-5t$, $R^2-c^2=16t(1-t)$, $\sqrt{R^2-c^2}=4\sqrt{t(1-t)}$, $dz=5\,dt$.

$$V_{\text{up}}=5\int_0^1\!\Big[(4-3t)^2\arccos\!\tfrac{4-5t}{4-3t}-4(4-5t)\sqrt{t(1-t)}\Big]dt=5\,[\,I_1-I_2\,].$$

### Evaluating $I_2$
$$I_2=4\!\int_0^1(4-5t)\sqrt{t(1-t)}\,dt=4\!\left[4\cdot\tfrac{\pi}{8}-5\cdot\tfrac{4}{15}\right]=4\!\left[\tfrac{\pi}{2}-\tfrac43\right]=2\pi-\tfrac{16}{3}.$$

### Evaluating $I_1$ (integration by parts)
Let $u=\arccos\!\tfrac{4-5t}{4-3t}$, $dv=(4-3t)^2dt$, so $v=-\tfrac{(4-3t)^3}{9}$. Since $\tfrac{d}{dt}\tfrac{4-5t}{4-3t}=\tfrac{-8}{(4-3t)^2}$ and $\sqrt{1-\cdot^2}=\tfrac{4\sqrt{t(1-t)}}{4-3t}$,
$$du=\frac{2}{(4-3t)\sqrt{t(1-t)}}\,dt.$$
Boundary terms: at $t=1$, $v\cdot u=(-\tfrac19)\pi$; at $t=0$, $v\cdot u=0$. Thus
$$I_1=-\frac{\pi}{9}+\frac{2}{9}\underbrace{\int_0^1\frac{(4-3t)^2}{\sqrt{t(1-t)}}\,dt}_{J}.$$
Expanding $(4-3t)^2=16-24t+9t^2$ and using $B$-integrals ($\pi,\;\tfrac\pi2,\;\tfrac{3\pi}{8}$):
$$J=16\pi-24\cdot\tfrac\pi2+9\cdot\tfrac{3\pi}{8}=4\pi+\tfrac{27\pi}{8}=\tfrac{59\pi}{8}.$$
$$I_1=-\frac{\pi}{9}+\frac{2}{9}\cdot\frac{59\pi}{8}=\frac{55\pi}{36}.$$

### Assembling
$$V_{\text{up}}=5\!\left[\frac{55\pi}{36}-2\pi+\frac{16}{3}\right]=5\cdot\frac{192-17\pi}{36}=\frac{5(192-17\pi)}{36}.$$

The total frustum volume is $V=\tfrac13\pi\cdot 5\,(16+4+1)=35\pi$, so
$$V_{\text{low}}=35\pi-\frac{5(192-17\pi)}{36}=\frac{1260\pi-960+85\pi}{36}=\frac{5(269\pi-192)}{36}.$$

## Result

$$\frac{V_{\text{up}}}{V_{\text{low}}}=\frac{5(192-17\pi)/36}{5(269\pi-192)/36}=\boxed{\dfrac{192-17\pi}{269\pi-192}}.$$

Numerically $\approx 0.2123$. (Sanity check: $V_{\text{up}}\approx 19.25$, $V_{\text{low}}\approx 90.69$, sum $\approx 109.94\approx 35\pi$. ✓)

I'll solve this problem directly. Let me work through it carefully.

## Setup

Place the frustum's axis along the $z$-axis: lower base is the disk $x^2+y^2\le 16$ at $z=0$ (radius 4), upper base is $x^2+y^2\le 1$ at $z=5$ (radius 1). The radius at height $z$ is $R(z)=4-\tfrac{3}{5}z$.

## Finding the cutting plane

By rotational symmetry, the plane (tangent to both base-disks and cutting all generators) can be taken parallel to the $y$-axis: $x=\alpha z+\beta$.

**Tangency to lower base** ($z=0$): the line $x=\beta$ must be tangent to the disk $x^2+y^2\le 16$, so $\beta=\pm 4$. Take $\beta=4$ (tangent point $(4,0,0)$).

**Tangency to upper base** ($z=5$): $x=5\alpha+4$ tangent to $x^2+y^2\le 1$, so $(5\alpha+4)^2=1$, giving $\alpha=-\tfrac35$ or $\alpha=-1$.

A generator at angle $\theta$ runs from $(4\cos\theta,4\sin\theta,0)$ to $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta,5)$, with $x(z)=\cos\theta\,(4-\tfrac35 z)$. The plane intersects it where
$$\cos\theta\,(4-\tfrac35 z)=\alpha z+4.$$

- **$\alpha=-\tfrac35$**: gives $(\cos\theta-1)(4-\tfrac35 z)=0$, so for $\theta\ne 0$ the only solution is $z=\tfrac{20}{3}\notin[0,5]$ — the plane is parallel to all generators, not cutting them. **Rejected.**
- **$\alpha=-1$**: gives $z=\dfrac{20(1-\cos\theta)}{5-3\cos\theta}\in[0,5]$ for all $\theta$ (equals $0$ at $\theta=0$, equals $5$ at $\theta=\pi$). **Cuts all elements.** ✓

So the plane is $\boxed{x+z=4}$.

## Computing the volumes

At height $z$, the cross-section is a disk of radius $R=4-\tfrac35 z$; the plane gives the line $x=4-z$. Set $c=4-z$. The **upper part** ($x+z\ge 4$, i.e. $x\ge c$) has circular-segment area
$$A_{\text{up}}(z)=R^2\arccos\!\tfrac{c}{R}-c\sqrt{R^2-c^2}.$$

Check regimes: $c-R=-\tfrac25 z<0$ for $z>0$ (always a right segment), $c+R=8(1-\tfrac z5)>0$ for $z<5$ (never the full disk). Good — segment regime throughout $(0,5)$.

Substitute $t=z/5\in[0,1]$: $R=4-3t$, $c=4-5t$, $R^2-c^2=16t(1-t)$, $\sqrt{R^2-c^2}=4\sqrt{t(1-t)}$, $dz=5\,dt$.

$$V_{\text{up}}=5\int_0^1\!\Big[(4-3t)^2\arccos\!\tfrac{4-5t}{4-3t}-4(4-5t)\sqrt{t(1-t)}\Big]dt=5\,[\,I_1-I_2\,].$$

### Evaluating $I_2$
$$I_2=4\!\int_0^1(4-5t)\sqrt{t(1-t)}\,dt=4\!\left[4\cdot\tfrac{\pi}{8}-5\cdot\tfrac{4}{15}\right]=4\!\left[\tfrac{\pi}{2}-\tfrac43\right]=2\pi-\tfrac{16}{3}.$$

### Evaluating $I_1$ (integration by parts)
Let $u=\arccos\!\tfrac{4-5t}{4-3t}$, $dv=(4-3t)^2dt$, so $v=-\tfrac{(4-3t)^3}{9}$. Since $\tfrac{d}{dt}\tfrac{4-5t}{4-3t}=\tfrac{-8}{(4-3t)^2}$ and $\sqrt{1-\cdot^2}=\tfrac{4\sqrt{t(1-t)}}{4-3t}$,
$$du=\frac{2}{(4-3t)\sqrt{t(1-t)}}\,dt.$$
Boundary terms: at $t=1$, $v\cdot u=(-\tfrac19)\pi$; at $t=0$, $v\cdot u=0$. Thus
$$I_1=-\frac{\pi}{9}+\frac{2}{9}\underbrace{\int_0^1\frac{(4-3t)^2}{\sqrt{t(1-t)}}\,dt}_{J}.$$
Expanding $(4-3t)^2=16-24t+9t^2$ and using $B$-integrals ($\pi,\;\tfrac\pi2,\;\tfrac{3\pi}{8}$):
$$J=16\pi-24\cdot\tfrac\pi2+9\cdot\tfrac{3\pi}{8}=4\pi+\tfrac{27\pi}{8}=\tfrac{59\pi}{8}.$$
$$I_1=-\frac{\pi}{9}+\frac{2}{9}\cdot\frac{59\pi}{8}=\frac{55\pi}{36}.$$

### Assembling
$$V_{\text{up}}=5\!\left[\frac{55\pi}{36}-2\pi+\frac{16}{3}\right]=5\cdot\frac{192-17\pi}{36}=\frac{5(192-17\pi)}{36}.$$

The total frustum volume is $V=\tfrac13\pi\cdot 5\,(16+4+1)=35\pi$, so
$$V_{\text{low}}=35\pi-\frac{5(192-17\pi)}{36}=\frac{1260\pi-960+85\pi}{36}=\frac{5(269\pi-192)}{36}.$$

## Result

$$\frac{V_{\text{up}}}{V_{\text{low}}}=\frac{5(192-17\pi)/36}{5(269\pi-192)/36}=\boxed{\dfrac{192-17\pi}{269\pi-192}}.$$

Numerically $\approx 0.2123$. (Sanity check: $V_{\text{up}}\approx 19.25$, $V_{\text{low}}\approx 90.69$, sum $\approx 109.94\approx 35\pi$. ✓)

### PROOF COMPLETE
